title: the-sentencing-process-guideline-d.pdf — section 9
text:
21. Aggravating factors are facts and circumstances which may make the offence more serious for
sentencing purposes. Mitigating factors, including factors personal to the offender, may lead to
a less severe sentence being imposed.

22. Cases may have both aggravating and mitigating factors. Whether any factor has an
aggravating or mitigating effect will depend on all of the circumstances of the case. Some
aggravating factors can be integral features of certain offences. In such cases, the court will
already have reflected this in assessing seriousness at step 1, and they should not be used as
a reason for further increasing the sentence.

23. Annex A lists some examples of statutory aggravations. When a statutory aggravation applies
to the case, the court must ensure that the requirements of the statute are followed.
